hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Switch from FM with pointwise loss to LightGBM with lambdarank and add item_agg features, using group_chunk=6 to match valid list length.
rationale: The baseline uses pointwise logloss but is scored on ranking metrics [POINTWISE_BASELINE]. LambdaRank directly optimises nDCG. Group_chunk=6 matches the ~5.6 rows/user in valid [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]. Item_agg provides continuous video/author popularity rates that vary within a user's list, which LightGBM can exploit efficiently for within-user ranking [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. Together these address the top-listed unexplored direction [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] Ranking loss directly optimises the scored metric, closing ~9% of the 0.247 gap to ceiling. [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] group_chunk=6 reduces train/valid list-length ratio from 7.8x to ~1.1x, eliminating a major domain shift. Item_agg adds within-user-varying continuous signal that LightGBM can exploit better than high-cardinality categoricals. Combined effect estimated at +0.022.

block_justifications.base5: Provides the core categorical identifiers (video_id, author_id, tab, dur_bucket) whose within-user variation is the basis for ranking; user_id is needed for grouping even though it is constant within user.
block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold video/author rates (long-view rate, click rate, impression count) are continuous features that vary across items within a user's list, giving LightGBM direct item-quality signal for within-user ranking [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
